text: Step 5 skips entries whose home directory is gone, but the rule does not say what a bare start does when every entry is skipped and one of them is named `default` (e.g. the only entry was created by `--workspace default --cwd X` and X was deleted). Creating another `default` would duplicate the workspace identity. Assumed: the skipped `default` is neither reused nor replaced; a new registry entry is created on the first free port from 4500 whose `ws-<port>` name is also free, and named `ws-<port>` (the step-3 fallback name). A later bare start selects that entry as the sole candidate.
assumption: ASSUMPTION:dev-0507 — with no candidate left and `default` taken by a skipped entry, the bare start creates registry workspace `ws-<port>` on the first free port whose `ws-<port>` name is free too.
